rounds.text: Sacheerome Ltd carries notable valuation and structural risks that the underlying evidence does not fully support, particularly regarding institutional conviction and asset efficiency. Institutional backing is actively eroding, with foreign institutions cutting holdings to 0.19% and domestic institutions slashing theirs to 6.27%, resulting in a net-negative institutional money flow signal [E30, E31, E32]. This severe flight of smart money directly contradicts the retail euphoria that has driven the share price up 147% over the past year and left it sitting at 80% of its 52-week range [E5, E18]. Furthermore, the company's asset-light narrative is strained by a return on assets (ROA) of 0%, which severely underperforms the sector benchmark of 5.86% [E8]. This disconnect is compounded by an aggressive capital expenditure cycle, evidenced by Capital Work-in-Progress (CWIP) surging 103.6% to Rs 57 Cr and a large debt-funded expansion including a ~Rs 60 Cr term loan from HDFC Bank, introducing execution and leverage risks [E28, E70, E71]. Conceded: the company boasts a pristine debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x, robust recent sales and profit growth, and high short-term returns on capital [E15, E17, E26, E47]. Nevertheless, the lack of any dividend payout combined with short-term quarterly operating margins that are flagged as inconsistent leaves investors bearing all the risk without immediate cash returns [E24, E42].

Conceded: foreign and domestic institutional holdings have declined alongside a negative money flow signal [E30, E31, E32]. However, the flight of institutional capital overlooks exceptional core profitability, as evidenced by an ROE of 27.0% and ROCE of 35.7% that comfortably outperform sector benchmarks [E9, E10, E13]. Conceded: the ROA of 0% lags the sector [E8]. Nevertheless, this metric fails to capture the immense productive asset build-up currently underway, where a 103.6% surge in CWIP to Rs 57 Cr represents massive future capacity expansion rather than operational failure [E28]. The upcoming YEIDA facility will expand total capacity to 2,760,000 kilos—nearly five times the current base—with management expecting more than 100% utilization starting in FY27 [E66, E67, E68]. While the ~Rs 60 Cr HDFC term loan funds this transformative growth, the company simultaneously maintains pristine financial health with borrowings at Rs 0 Cr as of Mar 2026 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x [E26, E27, E71]. Finally, the absence of dividends [E42] is entirely justified as management strategically reinvests internal accruals alongside IPO proceeds into a high-return expansion backed by resilient demand and sustainable EBITDA margin expansion of 26.98% [E57, E64, E69].

Conceded: the company maintains zero reported borrowings and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x as of March 2026 [E26, E27]. However, the bull ignores the massive emerging leverage burden, as management simultaneously details an active ~Rs 60 Cr term loan from HDFC Bank to finance the ongoing capital expenditure [E70, E71]. Conceded: the YEIDA facility aims to multiply capacity nearly five times [E66, E67]. Yet the projection of more than 100% capacity utilization starting in FY27 [E68] relies entirely on aggressive forward-looking assumptions that face acknowledged industry turbulences, including historical climatic scarcities, fires, and competitive pressures [E72, E73, E74]. Furthermore, while the bull defends the complete lack of dividends [E42] as strategic reinvestment, institutional investors are voting with their feet through a -1.27 percentage point drop in foreign holdings and a -6.54 percentage point drop in domestic holdings, generating a negative money flow signal [E30, E31, E32]. Finally, the claim of pristine asset productivity is heavily contradicted by an ROA of 0%, which severely lags the sector benchmark of 5.86% [E8].

Conceded: management details an active ~Rs 60 Cr term loan from HDFC Bank for the capital expenditure [E70, E71], but the company carries zero reported borrowings and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x as of March 2026 [E26, E27]. The bear’s concern over capacity utilization assumptions ignores that the company's current capacity of 7,60,000 kilos is expanding by 20 lakh kilos to reach 27,60,000 kilos [E66], backed by resilient demand across all categories and strong FMCG consumption [E57, E59]. Conceded: foreign and domestic institutional holdings saw recent percentage point drops and negative money flow [E30, E31, E32], but promoters maintain a dominant 71.54% stake with absolute stability [E29]. Conceded: an ROA of 0% is cited against the sector [E8], but this is completely contradicted by the company's elite core profitability metrics, including an ROE of 27.0% [E13], an ROCE of 35.7% [E12], and cash-backed operating profits where cash conversion reads 1.38x [E25].

Conceded: the company reports zero borrowings and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x as of March 2026 [E26, E27]. However, this zero-debt snapshot ignores the substantial financial commitments disclosed by management, including an active ~Rs 60 Cr term loan from HDFC Bank [E70, E71] and a massive capital expenditure push reflected in Capital Work in Progress surging 103.6% to Rs 57 Cr [E28]. While the bull points to a planned capacity expansion from 7,60,000 kilos to 27,60,000 kilos [E66], projecting "more than 100%" capacity utilization for FY27 [E68] rests on aggressive, unproven assumptions just as the industry faces severe structural turbulences, including climatic conditions causing raw material scarcity and historical supply disruptions from China products [E73]. Conceded: the bull highlights promoter stability at 71.54% [E29], but this fails to address the exodus of sophisticated capital, evidenced by foreign institutional holdings falling to 0.19% and domestic holdings dropping to 6.27% alongside negative money flow signals [E30, E31, E32]. Finally, dismissing the reported 0% return on assets [E8] relies entirely on high ROE and ROCE figures [E12, E13], yet recent operational momentum is already showing strain with quarterly operating margins turning inconsistent over the last two quarters [E24].
